item.title: [NH] NH Education Daily — Hot Off the Press: The Ballot Decisions That Will Reshape NH School Districts
item.description:
A one-hour breaking special, October 13, 2026: Three weeks before November 3, every NH voter faces Question 2 — the HB 1300 school tax cap. Alex and Jordan unpack what the ballot says vs. what RSA 32:5-i actually does, Londonderry's warning of million in cuts, district-by-district impacts from Hudson to Oyster River to Mascenic, the failed court challenges, and what real voters are posting on social media right now — verified posts from both sides. Plus: what a levy cap means for special education's unfunded mandates.

item.title: [NH] NH Education Deep Dive — Who's Teaching Special Ed? NH's Staffing Shortage
item.description:
The NH Fiscal Policy Institute's new report projects 1,114 teacher openings a year through 2034, with staffing down 5.7%, the pipeline halved, and teachers earning a third less than comparable professionals. Alex and Jordan unpack what it means for special education — endorsement barriers, the para crisis, the contracting trap, FAPE risk — and what districts can actually do about it.

item.title: [NH] NH Education Deep Dive — The Burden Shift: How HB 581 Rewrote the Rules of Special Ed Disputes in New Hampshire
item.description:
In 2021, New Hampshire moved the burden of proof in special education due process hearings off of parents and onto school districts. Alex and Jordan break down HB 581 — what changed, what it means for parents and districts, and what it demands of NH special education teams in their daily work. Educational guidance, not legal advice.
Work with our consultant One-on-one help for parents from an NH special education administrator: IEP reviews, meeting prep, Prior Written Notice — what to ask for, and how to ask for it. Consults $250 — book a consult: [link]
Sources - HB 581 as introduced (2021), full bill text (PDF), NH General Court archives: https://gencourt.state.nh.us/BillHistory/SofS_Archives/2021/house/HB581H.pdf - RSA 186-C:16-b, current text — Due Process Hearing; Appeal (see paragraph III-a), official NH General Court statute site: https://www.GenCourt.state.nh.us/rsa/html/XV/186-C/186-C-mrg.htm - "NH Changes Law Regarding Burden of Proof in Special Education Due Process Hearings," Disability Rights Center–New Hampshire, Aug 2, 2021: https://drcnh.org/statements/burden-of-proof-in-due-process-hearings/ - "Sununu signs bill shifting burden of proof in special education hearings to schools," Keene Sentinel (via NH Bulletin), 2021: https://www.keenesentinel.com/news/local/sununu-signs-bill-shifting-burden-of-proof-in-special-education-hearings-to-schools/article_78864d50-12bb-5eac-8d49-78cb31042cbf.html - NH Department of Education, FY26 "Rules and Laws in Excess" chart (PDF): http://doe.nhdoit.acsitefactory.com/sites/g/files/ehbemt326/files/inline-documents/sonh/fy26-nh-rules-and-laws-in-excess-chart.pdf - 2025 Compilation of Education Legislation, NH School Boards Association (PDF) — includes HB 754 (automatic discovery): https://nhsba.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2025-Compilation-of-Ed-Legislation-for-2025-Legislative-Summary.pdf - "New Hampshire Shifted the Due Process Burden to Schools in IEP Disputes.
